target.instruction: pick up the black bowl on the ramekin and place it on the plate

candidates.name: Support-Gated Lift for X-VLA
candidates.core_hypothesis: The repeated task5 failures are caused by insufficient support-separation behavior when the black bowl starts on the ramekin; a support-aware, observation-conditioned lift/regrasp phase can improve residual success without changing unrelated clean behavior.

inputs_allowed_at_inference: proprioception already available to the policy
mechanism.proposed_component: A small support-gate and residual action adapter that activates only when the scene/instruction indicates a bowl-on-support grasp. The activated phase biases the first one or two action chunks toward stable gripper closure, vertical clearance, and delayed lateral transport.
mechanism.why_not_r2p_xvla: R2P-XVLA phase-weighted task5 adaptation remains archived. SGL-XVLA is not a phase-weighted offline selector retune; it is a support-condition gate with a mechanism-specific lift/regrasp action prior that must be independently preregistered and tested.

candidates.claim_axis_if_developed: Increase success on the repeated task5 support-separation residual while retaining clean performance on X-VLA-solved task5 identities and non-task5 spatial controls.
required_future_gates_before_training: Freeze development identities and held-out confirmatory identities before any Ours rollout.
Build a no-training observability gate showing the support condition can be detected from allowed observations.
Build an offline action-shape sanity gate showing candidate outputs are finite, bounded, and do not require simulator state.
Define noninferiority margins for X-VLA-solved identities 20260731 and 20260732 before method execution.

base.scientific_question: Does SGL improve the frozen backbone on the repeated support-separation residual?
base.claim_metric: paired task success on frozen residual identities and held-out identities
base.blocking_condition: No practical success gain over Base or unacceptable clean degradation.
base.nonblocking_tradeoffs: Small added latency may be acceptable if residual success improves and clean retention stays inside the frozen margin.

closest_prior.scientific_question: Does SGL improve over X-VLA/OpenVLA under the same local protocol or offer a clear Pareto advantage?
closest_prior.claim_metric: paired residual success and clean-retention breakdown
closest_prior.blocking_condition: Matched official priors solve the held-out residuals or SGL fails to exceed them on the claim axis.
closest_prior.nonblocking_tradeoffs: Comparable success with lower intervention frequency or lower data could remain relevant if preregistered.

key_ablation.scientific_question: Is the support gate necessary, or does uniform residual adaptation explain the effect?
key_ablation.claim_metric: residual success difference between gated and ungated residual adapter
key_ablation.blocking_condition: Ungated/uniform adaptation matches or exceeds SGL across residual success, clean retention, and efficiency.
key_ablation.nonblocking_tradeoffs: Ungated may be slightly better on unrelated clean tasks if SGL is better on the support residual within frozen retention margins.

simple_control.scientific_question: Can a fixed lift primitive explain the gain?
simple_control.claim_metric: residual success and clean-retention vs fixed support-lift action template
simple_control.blocking_condition: The fixed lift template matches SGL at equal/lower cost without clean or generalization loss.
simple_control.nonblocking_tradeoffs: A fixed lift that solves one identity but fails held-out residual identities would not explain the mechanism.

primary_risks: The support gate may overfit visual appearance of the ramekin.
A simple fixed lift control may explain most gains.
Lift bias may degrade identities where X-VLA already succeeds.
candidates.recommended_next_step: Freeze a no-training Stage 0 specification and observability gate for SGL-XVLA.

candidates.name: Observation-Consistency Retry for X-VLA
candidates.core_hypothesis: The residual may be a recoverable grasp-progress failure: if the bowl does not visually/proprioceptively separate from the ramekin after an initial attempt, an observation-consistency retry can re-center and regrasp without privileged state.

inputs_allowed_at_inference: proprioception already available to the policy
mechanism.proposed_component: A lightweight retry monitor that checks observation/action consistency after the first grasp/lift attempt. If progress is absent under a frozen observation-only criterion, it triggers one bounded re-center/regrasp retry before returning control to the base policy.
mechanism.why_not_closed_methods: OCR-XVLA is not an archived phase-weighting, memory, routing, or closed residual method. It is a retry-monitor candidate that must be independently preregistered.

candidates.claim_axis_if_developed: Improve task5 residual success by recovering from failed first attempts while adding at most one bounded retry and preserving X-VLA successes on nonresidual identities.
required_future_gates_before_training: Freeze the observation-only no-progress criterion before any Ours rollout.
Verify the criterion does not use reward, simulator state, or reset identity.
Run a no-training replay/trace audit on existing failure logs to determine whether the retry trigger is observable.
Freeze a simple timeout retry control as the strongest plausible explanation.

base.scientific_question: Does OCR improve the backbone by recovering from repeated task5 first-attempt failures?
base.claim_metric: paired residual success and intervention count
base.blocking_condition: No residual success gain or excessive intervention frequency.
base.nonblocking_tradeoffs: A small latency increase may be acceptable if intervention count is bounded and success improves.

closest_prior.scientific_question: Does OCR produce a meaningful matched advantage over X-VLA/OpenVLA on the residual?
closest_prior.claim_metric: paired residual success and clean retention
closest_prior.blocking_condition: Official priors match OCR on residual success without the retry mechanism.
closest_prior.nonblocking_tradeoffs: Comparable success with lower training data could be relevant only if preregistered.

key_ablation.claim_metric: residual success vs always-retry and never-retry ablations
key_ablation.blocking_condition: Always-retry or never-retry matches OCR with lower complexity and no clean cost.
key_ablation.nonblocking_tradeoffs: Always-retry may solve one identity but still be inferior if it harms clean identities or efficiency.

simple_control.scientific_question: Can a trivial timeout retry explain the gain?
simple_control.claim_metric: residual success, clean retention, latency, and intervention count
simple_control.blocking_condition: A fixed timeout retry matches OCR at equal/lower cost and no missing mechanism.
simple_control.nonblocking_tradeoffs: A timeout retry that only works on development identities is not sufficient if OCR generalizes to held-out residuals.

primary_risks: The no-progress criterion may be hard to observe from allowed sensors.
A trivial fixed retry may explain the effect.
Extra retries may disturb clean X-VLA-solved identities.
candidates.recommended_next_step: Keep OCR-XVLA as backup until SGL-XVLA fails its no-training observability gate or the residual traces show clearer retry than support-separation structure.

frozen_development_boundary_for_next_sta.note: The held-out pool is proposed for the next preregistration; no Ours result has been run on these identities.

next_action: Create a frozen no-training Stage 0 specification/gate for the primary candidate SGL-XVLA. Do not train, write checkpoints, or run Ours.
